correctness.rationale: The proof gives an explicit two-way bijection between maximal independent vertex sets of a full edge subdivision and original-vertex subsets U that are empty or induce no isolated vertices; its weight is v-|U|+|E(G[U])|. The biclique formula, support, exact extrema, and gap interval follow by elementary exhaustive counting over shore sizes. The density statement correctly imports Ford’s Corollary 3. Separate definition-based enumeration checked 715550 biclique subsets, 1783 arbitrary-graph subsets, and 136 larger parameter-pair supports; the finite checks corroborate but do not prove the infinite result.

originality.rationale: Inspected 2021 full subdivision-number paper and 2018 independent-domination-polynomial primary full text, as well as Ford’s original multiplication-table Corollary 3, and compared claims to 124 accessible prior records and targeted published-finding corpus/web searches. Prior ordinary-domination work covers the minimum-size coefficient and is explicitly not claimed as new; it does not determine the complete maximal-independent-set distribution. Ford covers the analytic multiplication-table estimate, not the exact graph-theoretic identification. No equivalent complete biclique polynomial or support was identified, with unindexed literature acknowledged as residual risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent special-family graph polynomial may exist in unindexed or inaccessible prior literature despite targeted searches.
The general subdivision transform may be implicit in broader maximum independent set descriptions not found by this research.
Ford’s asymptotic is imported, not independently re-proved; its citation is essential.

value.rationale: The new all-coefficient polynomial for fully subdivided bicliques reveals a precise correspondence between independent domination cardinalities and distinct multiplication-table entries. It proves a natural infinite family of long forbidden cardinality intervals and a support density tending to zero, structurally beyond previously known minimum dominating sets or the graph-subdivision budget. This is a complete infinite-family classification rather than an arbitrary finite test or routine scalar increment.
